text: Each DASS-21 subscale score is the sum of its seven items (each item 0 to 3) multiplied by two, so scores are even values from 0 to 42. Depression items: 3, 5, 10, 13, 16, 17, 21. Anxiety items: 2, 4, 7, 9, 15, 19, 20. Stress items: 1, 6, 8, 11, 12, 14, 18.

Severity bands on the doubled score (Lovibond and Lovibond, 1995). Depression: Normal 0-9, Mild 10-13, Moderate 14-20, Severe 21-27, Extremely Severe 28+. Anxiety: Normal 0-7, Mild 8-9, Moderate 10-14, Severe 15-19, Extremely Severe 20+. Stress: Normal 0-14, Mild 15-18, Moderate 19-25, Severe 26-33, Extremely Severe 34+.

Platform requirement 6.2: the flag PERLU_PERHATIAN and a Crisis_Alerts entry are created automatically when the Depression category is Severe or Extremely Severe, or when item 10, 17, or 21 (hopelessness and worthlessness items) is scored 3.

Platform requirement 6.3: access to the text and voice companions is granted only to students whose most recent DASS-21 result is Normal on all three subscales. Students who never completed DASS-21 are not eligible.

Testing note (Article 1): because scores are even, a published odd cut-point c has no attainable score c-1 or c; boundary values must be the largest attainable score below c, L(c), and the smallest attainable score at or above c, U(c).

Testing note (Article 1): the flag is a disjunction of a category condition and an item condition; a test whose depression score reaches Severe may also set a critical item to 3, which hides faults in either condition. Each condition must be exercised alone.
Testing note (Article 1): build item responses for a target score with a rotating filling order, so that the load moves to different items across test cases and item-mapping faults are detected.
Fault taxonomy: threshold (cut-point shifted), scaling (wrong multiplier), item mapping (item counted on the wrong subscale), gate (eligibility rule wrong), flag (escalation rule wrong).
